newsitem.title: USA: Witness in Cosby son's killing is traumatized.
newsitem.headline: Witness in Cosby son's killing is traumatized.

text.p: The woman who witnessed the murder of entertainer Bill Cosby's son is so traumatized she has not yet been able to provide police with a detailed description of the killer, the Los Angeles police chief said on Friday.

As a result, there has been a delay in producing a composite sketch of the gunman who shot Ennis Cosby early on Thursday morning as he changed a tire alongside a freeway, Police Chief Willie Williams told reporters.
"Right now we're working with one witness, and the lady is traumatized," Williams said at a news conference.
He said the woman's fears resulted not only from having seen "some portion of the homicide", but from the enormous media attention focused on her since the murder.
Police Cmdr. Tim McBride told the Los Angeles Times the woman was "freaking out," fearing that the killer might retaliate against her.
Williams said police sketch artists met the woman on Thursday and on Friday and still hoped they could come up with a drawing of the killer, described only as a white man.

The woman, whose identity has been guarded by authorities, summoned police after the murder and was questioned extensively. Some television stations broadcast pictures of her standing near the crime scene wearing a short skirt and a fur coat and talking to police.
Asked if the woman knew the 27-year-old victim, Williams declined to comment.

But the Los Angeles Times cited sources as saying she was a friend of Ennis Cosby's and that he was on the way to meet her when he stopped to change a tire on a remote stretch of road in the fashionable Bel-Air neighbourhood.
Citing a highly placed source, the newspaper said Ennis Cosby called her on his cellular telephone to come to his aid and shine her car's headlights on his Mercedes convertible while he worked.

Williams' news conference came as the Los Angeles County coroner's office concluded an autopsy on the body of Ennis Cosby. Coroner's spokesman Scott Carrier said the man died of a single gunshot wound to the head. Autopsies are routinely carried out in murder cases, he said.

The dead man's parents and family were in seclusion, their whereabouts unknown after they left their Manhattan home late on Thursday. Bill Cosby's publicist, David Brokaw, said they had no plans to fly to Los Angeles and were still "back East." There was speculation they may have gone to the Cosby home in western Massachusetts.
The family also issued a statement appealing to the news media to stop staking out their homes and instead allow them to grieve in private.

Investigators believe robbery was the likely motive, but when asked about that theory on ABC's "Good Morning America," Williams said earlier: "We don't know ... We know what was left and what was taken, if something was taken.
"The vehicle obviously was not taken and the perpetrator was only there for a few moments or a few seconds ... but we don't know what was in his mind at this point in time."
"We have detectives working almost 24 hours a day now," the police chief said.

But at his news conference, the police chief stressed that the Cosby killing had no higher police priority than either of the other two murders in Los Angeles on Thursday -- an 18-year-old girl shot on a school bus during a gang fight and a woman who had been missing and was found shot to death in her San Fernando Valley home.
